name: The Plane Tree of Kozy

location.address: Park pałacowy (palace park) beside the Czeczów de Lindenwald Palace, ul. Bielska, Kozy, Bielsko County, Silesian Voivodeship, Poland
location.neighbourhood: Kozy village centre (roughly 18 km from Żywiec)

access: Free, in a public palace park in the centre of Kozy, right by the main road (route 52 / ul. Bielska). The park hosts community events (concerts, gatherings, competitions) around the tree, so it is open ground rather than a fenced private estate.
transport: About 18 km from central Żywiec by road (route 52, the Bielsko-Biała to Żywiec corridor), roughly 25 minutes by car; a day-trip stop by car rather than a walk from Żywiec's own tree. Regional buses run this corridor; no dedicated stop at the park confirmed.
verify_notes: 2013 European Tree of the Year, rank 2, 13,989 votes (beaten only by a plane tree in Eger, Hungary). Won Poland's own national 'Drzewo Roku' (Tree of the Year) contest first, in 2012, run by Klub Gaja: 7,044 of nearly 31,000 votes cast across 11 finalists, edging out a lime tree in Wambierzyce by just 128 votes; that win qualified it for the European final. Species: London Plane, Platanus x hispanica (= P. x acerifolia, same hybrid, canonical common name per hard rule 9); Polish sources call it 'platan klonolistny'. Legally protected as a 'pomnik przyrody' (nature monument), confirmed independently by Bielsko County's own heritage listing (powiat.bielsko.pl), which places it in the park surrounding the Czeczow (Czecz de Linewald) palace, alongside a fountain and ice-house ruins, all part of a landscaped estate whose park dates to the mid-18th century. Measurements per fotopolska.eu (a Polish historical/topographic photo archive, independent of both contest organisers): girth 482 cm, height about 16 m; age given everywhere as 'about 200 years' or 'over 200 years', with one source suggesting a planting date around 1836, which sits within that range rather than contradicting it -- treated as a rough consensus rather than a precise figure. STORY: the trunk is not a single stem but several seedlings planted together on purpose from the start and grown into one another, so the mature crown looks, in the contest's own words, like 'a wind-rose'; nobody today knows who the gardener was that planned it that way. In the past a fine plane tree like this signalled the wealth and connections of the landowner; today the tree has become the namesake of Kozy's own 'Platan' honorary award, given to people who have shaped the village's development. It remains a working community space: the park around it hosts concerts, competitions, gatherings and is a well-known meeting spot for couples and children, described the same way in both the 2013 contest text and a modern Polish tourism guide (polskieszlaki.pl), which also confirms the park sits right on the main road through Kozy and that events are still held there. DISTANCE CAVEAT for the writer: Kozy is roughly 18 km from Żywiec's own tree (zyw_001) and is arguably closer in character to Bielsko-Biała than to Żywiec; the page should name Kozy honestly as its own village and state the real driving distance rather than imply it is a short stroll from central Żywiec.
